how_it_wins:
The table reads {5}{R}{G}{W} and files you under later. The goldfish says otherwise: Gishath, Sun's Avatar has a mean cast turn of 7.362, lands by turn six in 25.5% of games, and never lands by turn ten in 2,299 of 10,000. Every turn before him is THE EIGHT-MANA CLIMB, and it is not a waiting room.

He is the whole engine. Three cards make the command-zone cast cheaper — Otepec Huntmaster {1}, Urza's Incubator {2}, Knight of the Stampede {2} — and all three together leave exactly {R}{G}{W}. Then THE FIRST CONNECTION: vigilance, trample and haste are printed on him, so the kit's job is a clear lane (Rogue's Passage, Kessig Wolf Run) and a bigger hit (Enlarge is +7/+7, a fourteen-card reveal). Forge, 40 games against sythis, jarad and abaddon: 60 attacks, 42 reveals, 0.70 per attack. At that rate the goldfish fires the reveal 1.953 times a game for 4.096 free Dinosaurs.

Stack 001 is what one seven-damage hit buys: four Dinosaurs off the top enter as one event, three cards off Garruk's Uprising, one Pantlaza discover at X=6 — and X=6 only because you stack the Regisaur Alpha token trigger last. That is A CARD PER DINOSAUR, and it is the only verified arrow that starts from him.

The enrage web is gone. What is left is two converters, Trapjaw Tyrant and Wrathful Raptors, and one card that damages your own board without a mana cost per hit, Blasphemous Act. Read the pair for what it is: the Act through Temple Altisaur is a one-sided 13 (stack 004) that arrives in 8.1% of games unassisted, 29.9% with a tutor. An answer to a wide table, not a plan.

What the table misreads: you deploy in one wave, so one sweeper takes the board and the dorks under it. Kill by turn 8 is 0.617 against a goldfish with no blockers; with blockers, Forge gave 12 wins in 35 decided games. Hold Flawless Maneuver over the tap-out turn — with him on the battlefield it costs nothing.

combo_lines.001:
The clause that decides this is CR 603.2h: an ability reading 'Do this only once each turn' triggers only if its controller has not already taken that action this turn. Pantlaza, Sun-Favored triggers four times off one simultaneous entry and discovers exactly once.

CR 603.3b puts your triggers on the stack in any order; CR 405.5 resolves the top one first. Carnage Tyrant's trigger on top is a discover at X=6. Regisaur Alpha's token trigger resolving earlier spends the action on a 3-toughness token, and the later triggers do not trigger at all.

Garruk's Uprising is arithmetic. CR 603.2c lets one event trigger an ability once per qualifying occurrence: three of the four enterers have power 4 or greater; the 3/4 and the 3/3 token do not.

The stipulated reveal is the list as it stood when this resolved: Ripjaw Raptor and Cultivate have since left the 99. The holding depends on power and toughness, not on which Dinosaurs come up.

The holding: four Dinosaur creature cards enter, three cards are drawn, one discover resolves, at X=6 only because it resolved before the token existed.
combo_lines.004:
The clause is three words on Temple Altisaur: 'another Dinosaur you control.' Altisaur is not another Dinosaur relative to itself, so its shield covers every other Dinosaur you control and not itself.

CR 615.1 sets the timing — prevention applies as the damage event happens — so what matters downstream is the amount actually dealt: 13 to Altisaur, 1 to each other Dinosaur.

CR 704.3 has state-based actions destroy every lethally damaged creature before the waiting triggers go on the stack, and CR 115.1d chooses targets as they go on. By then the opponents' creatures are in graveyards; the only legal non-Dinosaur targets left are players. The dead Altisaur still pays: CR 113.7a lets its 13 fire a redirect on last known information.

Ripjaw Raptor's draw left with Ripjaw. The 99 converts that 1 through Wrathful Raptors, on this board, and through Trapjaw Tyrant, which is not on it; its exile off the same 1 is unresolved.

The holding: three Dinosaurs are dealt 1 each and survive, and the redirects total 16 at one opponent — 26 down to 10. A one-sided sweep, not a kill.

card_roles.Gishath, Sun's Avatar: Do not swing him for value — swing him with a lane cleared or a shield in hand, because stack 001 prices one seven-damage connection at four Dinosaurs off the top, three cards and a discover. Every trip back to the command zone adds {2} to an already eight-mana bill, so make the first hit the one that matters.
card_roles.Akroma's Will: With your commander anywhere on the battlefield you take both halves: protection from each colour to walk past blockers and removal, double strike to finish. Save it for the turn you are attacking and being answered in the same breath.
card_roles.Alpine Meadow: Red-white snow tapland. It goes down on a turn you were not spending anyway, never the turn before your commander.
card_roles.Arcane Signet: Any colour you need on turn two with no strings attached. Play it over a second tapland every single time.
card_roles.Austere Command: You pick which two halves land, so aim it at the modes your own board survives — artifacts and enchantments, or the small creatures while your fat lives. Cast it before you commit your hand, not after.
card_roles.Beast Within: Your only answer to a land and an instant-speed answer to anything else on the table. Hand over the 3/3 without flinching; you are the deck with the bigger board.
card_roles.Belbe's Portal: Name Dinosaur and put one from hand straight onto the battlefield for {3} — your way around a counterspell or a wrath turn. It does nothing for the commander in the command zone, and Unclaimed Territory's mana cannot pay for the activation.
card_roles.Blasphemous Act: Nine creatures on the table makes it cost {R}. Check for Temple Altisaur first: with the Altisaur down your Dinosaurs take 1 each and everyone else's die (stack 004).
card_roles.Bonehoard Dracosaur: A flying first-striker that exiles two cards off your library every upkeep and leaves you a 3/1 or a Treasure. This is upkeep card advantage — nothing about it converts a ping, so do not count it as part of the web.
card_roles.Boros Charm: Four damage, indestructible across all your permanents, or double strike — read the turn and pick. The indestructible mode is your cheapest out to a sweeper.
card_roles.Boros Signet: Both of your short colours out of one rock. Get it down early, because red and white are the mana you will actually be missing.
card_roles.Bronzebeak Foragers: One body that answers a nonland permanent per opponent, and a Dinosaur, so the commander can free-roll it onto the battlefield. The exile only lasts while it lives — protect it or expect everything back.
card_roles.Canopy Vista: Green-white, untapped once two basics are down. Lead on basics and this is a real dual by turn three.
card_roles.Carnage Tyrant: The threat you deploy into open blue mana — uncounterable, hexproof, trample. Cast him first when a control seat is holding up two.
card_roles.Cinder Glade: Red-green battle land, same rule as Canopy Vista: two basics first and it comes in untapped.
card_roles.City of Brass: Any colour for one life a tap. In a deck sitting 16 sources short in red and white, pay the life and stop thinking about it.
card_roles.Clifftop Retreat: Untapped if you already control a Mountain or a Plains — which is exactly the board state where you want red and white.
card_roles.Command Tower: All three colours, untapped, free. It is the first land you play out of any keep.
card_roles.Congregation at Dawn: Instant speed, three creature cards stacked on top in the order you choose, which is the commander's reveal loaded in advance. Do it on the end step before your swing, not on your own main phase.
card_roles.Cultivate: Turn-three ramp that fixes at the same time: one basic to the battlefield, one to hand. It is a big part of why your turn-six land drop still happens.
card_roles.Curious Altisaur: Any Dinosaur connecting draws you a card, not just the big one, so it pays on a wide board rather than a tall one. Vigilance and reach mean it blocks while it earns.
card_roles.Descendants' Path: A free Dinosaur off the top every upkeep, and 29 of your creature copies are Dinosaurs. Land it on turn three and let it hit twice before anyone bothers answering it.
card_roles.Eerie Interlude: The one shield in the deck that beats a non-targeted mass exile, and it re-buys every enters-the-battlefield trigger on the way back. Hold it against the seat that exiles rather than destroys.
card_roles.Enlightened Tutor: Point it at Urza's Incubator when you need the commander cheaper and Garruk's Uprising when you need cards. It puts the card on top, so cast it on their end step and pay the tempo a turn early.
card_roles.Etali, Primal Storm: Attack with him and the top card of every library is yours to cast for free. He does not need to connect — he only needs to attack, so send him into a board that will block him.
card_roles.Exotic Orchard: Whatever your opponents' lands can make. At a three-colour table that is everything; against one mono-coloured seat, plan around it.
card_roles.Flawless Maneuver: Free while you control a commander, which makes it the only protection you can hold on the turn you tap out for eight. Never spend it as a combat trick when a sweeper is live.
card_roles.Forbidden Orchard: Any colour, and the opponent gets a 1/1 Spirit. Tap it when you need the fixing, and remember you just handed the table a blocker — and Trapjaw Tyrant a target.
card_roles.Forest: Seven copies, and the card every fetch effect in the deck is hunting. Lead on basics to switch on the battle lands and check lands.
card_roles.Garruk's Uprising: Trample for the whole board plus a card for every power-4 body that lands — three draws off one connection in stack 001. Get it down before the commander, not after.
card_roles.Ghalta and Mavren: Attack and choose: one enormous trampling token, or a row of lifelinking Vampires. Take the token when you need to punch through, the row when you need bodies.
card_roles.Ghalta, Primal Hunger: He costs {X} less for your total power, so on a real board he is a four-mana 12/12. Cast him after the board exists, never in front of it.
card_roles.Heroic Intervention: Two mana buys hexproof and indestructible across everything you own, which answers targeted removal and sweepers with one card. It is the cheapest insurance policy in the 99.
card_roles.Huatli, Poet of Unity // Roar of the Fif: The front face fetches a basic to hand and holds the ground; flip her when you have {3}{R/W}{R/W} spare and the Saga makes two 3/3s, turns your creatures into mana, tutors a Dinosaur, then hands out double strike and trample. Flip on a turn where chapter IV will find an attack.
card_roles.Hulking Raptor: Two green at the start of every one of your main phases, with ward {2} making it awkward to answer cheaply. Turn-four Raptor into a turn-five six-drop is the line.
card_roles.Hunter's Insight: Point it at whatever is unblocked and draw that many cards. The commander is the dream target; any trampler will do the job.
card_roles.Intrepid Paleontologist: A dork that fixes all three colours, exiles graveyards for {2}, and lets you cast the Dinosaurs it exiled. It is your only graveyard answer — do not trade it away for nothing.
card_roles.Itzquinth, Firstborn of Gishath: Two mana, haste, and an enters trigger that pays {2} to have a Dinosaur deal its power to another creature. Point that at your own board when you want the enrage payouts instead of the kill.
card_roles.Jetmir's Garden: All three colours, always tapped, and it cycles for {3} when you are flooded. Land it on a cheap turn and forget about it.
card_roles.Kessig Wolf Run: Colourless most turns, and a mana sink that adds power and trample to an attacker. Save the activation for the connection that has to get there.
card_roles.Kodama's Reach: Cultivate under a different name. Same turn, same job, same reason to be happy to see it.
card_roles.Krosan Verge: It enters tapped and costs {2} to crack, but it fetches a Forest and a Plains — the two land types this mana base is shortest on. Fire it on a turn you were not casting anything.
card_roles.Mirari's Wake: Every land taps for double and your creatures get +1/+1. It is the fastest route from five lands to an eight-drop that does not involve a creature you can lose.
card_roles.Monster Manual // Zoological Study: Cast the Adventure early to dig five deep for a creature; the artifact later puts one from hand onto the battlefield for {1}{G} a turn. Neither half discounts the commander, so do not file it under ignition.
card_roles.Mountain: Four copies against 19 red pips. It is the basic you are most often missing when Blasphemous Act is sitting in hand.
card_roles.Myriad Landscape: Enters tapped, then trades itself for two basics that share a type. Crack it on the turn you would otherwise miss a land drop.
card_roles.Nature's Lore: Two mana, a Forest onto the battlefield, and five of your nonbasics carry the Forest type — Canopy Vista, Cinder Glade, Arctic Treeline, Commercial District and Jetmir's Garden. Take a dual over a basic whenever you need the second colour more than the basic count.
card_roles.Otepec Huntmaster: One of exactly two cards in the 99 that make your commander cheaper from the command zone, and it grants a Dinosaur haste on top. Play it on turn two and keep it alive.
card_roles.Overwhelming Stampede: Everything gains trample and grows by your greatest power. Hold it for the turn the board is already wide, not the turn you wish it were.
card_roles.Pantlaza, Sun-Favored: Once each turn a Dinosaur entering discovers X equal to its toughness — free cards with no combat step attached. When several enter at once, resolve the biggest-toughness trigger first; stack 001 shows the window closing on a 3/3 token if you don't.
card_roles.Path of Ancestry: Enters tapped, then scries every time its mana casts a Dinosaur. A small edge every turn for one slow land is a trade you take.
card_roles.Path to Exile: One mana, exiled, they get a basic. Spend it on the enabler that beats you, not the biggest body on the table.
card_roles.Plains: Three copies against Wakening Sun's Avatar's {W}{W}{W}. Fetch them early rather than hoping the top of your library agrees with you.
card_roles.Pugnacious Hammerskull: A 6/6 for three mana, and that is the whole pitch — the stun counter only bites when you attack with no other Dinosaur out, which is rare here. It converts no damage; it simply hits hard.
card_roles.Quartzwood Crasher: Every point of trample damage you push through becomes an X/X Dinosaur token. Garruk's Uprising gives the rest of your board trample, so land the two together and one attack builds the next board.
card_roles.Regal Imperiosaur: A 5/4 for three that grows every other Dinosaur you own. It is the cheapest way to push a wide board past blockers.
card_roles.Regisaur Alpha: Haste for every other Dinosaur, which is what turns the commander's reveal into an attack, plus a 3/3 on arrival. When it arrives off the trigger, resolve that token last.
card_roles.Ripjaw Raptor: Every point of damage dealt to it draws a card — your own Forerunner ping and your own Blasphemous Act included. It is a 4/5, so let it get hit.
card_roles.Rishkar's Expertise: Draw cards equal to your greatest power, then cast something for free. With the commander out that is seven cards; without him it is still four or five.
card_roles.Rogue's Passage: Four mana makes anything unblockable, which is the cleanest guarantee of a commander connection you own. Keep the mana up on the turn you intend to swing.
card_roles.Rootbound Crag: Untapped once you control a Mountain or a Forest, which is most turns from three onward.
card_roles.Secluded Courtyard: Name Dinosaur. Its coloured mana casts your Dinosaurs and pays for their activated abilities; the colourless mode covers everything else. Use it on Belbe's Portal and Monster Manual without hesitating.
card_roles.Skyshroud Claim: Two Forests onto the battlefield untapped, and any Forest-typed dual qualifies. It is the best mana turn in the deck.
card_roles.Sol Ring: Sol Ring. There is no turn on which you are unhappy to see it.
card_roles.Sunpetal Grove: Untapped once you control a Forest or a Plains — your green-white fix from turn three onward.
card_roles.Swords to Plowshares: One mana and it is gone. Save it for the creature that ends you, not the one that annoys you.
card_roles.Talisman of Unity: Green and white for a life, or colourless for free. The white half matters more than it looks in a deck holding 20 white sources.
card_roles.Temple Altisaur: Not a damage payoff — a damage floor. Everything hitting your other Dinosaurs is prevented down to 1, which is precisely what makes your own Blasphemous Act one-sided (stack 004). It shields neither itself nor Forerunner of the Empire, who is a Human.
card_roles.Thrashing Brontodon: A Dinosaur body that doubles as an artifact or enchantment answer for {1}. Do not sacrifice it on turn four for something you could ignore — the body is doing real work.
card_roles.Topiary Stomper: It is a ramp spell first and a 4/4 only once you control seven lands. Cast it on turn three for the land and be pleasantly surprised later.
card_roles.Triumphant Chomp: One red mana, damage equal to your greatest Dinosaur's power. Point it at a blocker, or at your own Ripjaw Raptor when the card is worth more to you than the kill.
card_roles.Trumpeting Carnosaur: Discover 5 on arrival, trample on the body, and it can be discarded for {2}{R} to shoot something for 3. Card advantage and removal in one slot — no part of it converts damage on your own board.
card_roles.Unclaimed Territory: Name Dinosaur and it casts your creatures in any colour. Its coloured mana cannot pay an activation cost, so leave it out of the maths when you are lining up Belbe's Portal or Monster Manual.
card_roles.Urza's Incubator: Takes {2} off every Dinosaur creature spell including the one in the command zone, and it is one of only two cards in the 99 that reach that cast. That is the difference between a turn-eight commander and a turn-six one.
card_roles.Vaultborn Tyrant: Three life and a card for every power-4 body that lands, which is most of yours, and it leaves a copy behind when it dies. If you are drawing exactly one card late, this is the one to want.
card_roles.Wakening Sun's Avatar: Cast it from your hand and every non-Dinosaur creature on the table dies. Off the commander's trigger it is only a body, so pay the {5}{W}{W}{W} on the turn the sweep is the point.
card_roles.Wayward Swordtooth: An extra land drop every turn, which is the single most direct attack on a turn-eight commander. It cannot attack or block until you control ten permanents, and you will not care.
card_roles.Worldly Tutor: Instant speed, any creature, on top of your library. Cast it on their end step so the card is in hand when your turn starts.
card_roles.Zacama, Primal Calamity: Nine mana that untaps your lands on the way in, so he usually pays for his own abilities the turn he arrives. {2}{R} for 3 damage is expensive, but it is a repeatable damage source your enrage cards can eat.
card_roles.Selvala, Heart of the Wilds: She taps for mana equal to your greatest power, so with one 5/5 out she is a five-mana land. She is your fastest honest route to an eight-drop, and everyone who reads her knows it — expect her to be answered.
card_roles.Regal Behemoth: The monarch, plus an extra mana every time you tap a land. Both halves are excellent and both halves paint a target on you, so take the crown on a turn you can defend it.
card_roles.Forerunner of the Empire: The switch for the entire enrage web: every Dinosaur entering lets you ping the whole board for 1, free, with no combat step. Its arrival also stacks a Dinosaur on top of your library. It is a 1/3 Human that no tribal shield in this deck covers, so cover it with the board-wide instants or lose it cheaply.
card_roles.Polyraptor: Every point of damage dealt to it makes another copy, and every copy entering re-arms Forerunner of the Empire. Stack 003 caps that chain at seven tokens and every link is a choice you are allowed to decline.
card_roles.Wrathful Raptors: Damage to any Dinosaur you control becomes that much damage at any non-Dinosaur target, which usually means a face. It is the card that turns the web from value into reach.
card_roles.Ranging Raptors: One point of damage fetches a basic land onto the battlefield tapped. Take the land every time the web fires — a land is banked where a token is not.
card_roles.Trapjaw Tyrant: One point of damage exiles a creature an opponent controls, repeatedly, for free. The hostage returns the moment the Tyrant leaves, so protect it or make the trade with your eyes open.
card_roles.Windswept Heath: One life for a Forest or a Plains, untapped, aimed at the colours you are shortest in. Crack it on their end step unless you need the land type right now.
card_roles.Commercial District: Red-green tapland with a surveil attached. Play it on a turn you had spare mana anyway.
card_roles.Arctic Treeline: Green-white snow tapland. Same rule as the rest of them: it goes down on the cheap turns, never the turn before your commander.

mulligan:
Opening sevens keep 78.0% of the time and a game costs you 0.271 mulligans. 398 of 10,000 first sevens hold zero lands and 1,721 hold one; ship those, and no Dinosaur changes it.

The keep: two to four lands and one card that moves mana before turn four. Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Boros Signet, Talisman of Unity, Nature's Lore, Kodama's Reach, Skyshroud Claim, Topiary Stomper, Wayward Swordtooth — any one of them and the hand acts by turn three, which 83.7% of kept hands do.

A reducer outranks a rock. Otepec Huntmaster, Urza's Incubator and Knight of the Stampede are the only three cards that make a command-zone cast cheaper; each is 7.1% of an opening seven, and the 25.5% commander-by-turn-six figure rests on drawing one. Keep any two-land hand with a reducer and a Dinosaur to cast on four. Knight is a Human, so the reveal never gives it to you; a drawn Knight is a kept Knight.

Ship the top end. Zacama, Primal Calamity, Wakening Sun's Avatar, Ghalta, Primal Hunger and Blasphemous Act with no ramp under them is a second act with no first act. Five cards in this list cost eight or more and one of them is your commander; never keep two of the others on faith.

Ship the converters. Trapjaw Tyrant and Wrathful Raptors turn damage on your own Dinosaurs into exile and reach, and nothing in the 99 supplies that damage for free: the Act is a card, Zacama's ping is {2}{R}, Itzquinth's is {2}. A hand of both converters is two blanks. They land by turn six in 28.1% of games as it is; do not mulligan toward them either.

The hand to keep on sight: a land-ramp sorcery, a reducer and a five-drop Dinosaur. That is the climb, the discount and the first body. The reveal does the rest.
upgrades:
Ten cards, and the mean mana value is 2.5. That is the first honest thing to say about a short list assembled for a deck whose headline card costs eight and which already carries six entries at mana value 8 or more. Nothing here is trying to out-top-end the top end.

Sort them by the axis each one names and the shape falls straight out: three go at colour sources, three widen the damage class the enrage web runs on, two buy ignition, one buys curve, and one closes nothing the audit measures at all. Colour sources is the axis reading 16 short at its worst colour, so three picks aimed there is the list agreeing with the audit rather than arguing with it.

The popularity spread is the fun number. It runs from EDHREC rank 23 to rank 6,977 — a factor of three hundred on the same page. Farseek at 23 and Birds of Paradise at 33 are cards half of Commander already plays. Knight of the Stampede at 6,977 is a card almost nobody plays, because almost nobody has this exact problem: a {2} discount on Dinosaur spells specifically. Both ends of that range are here for the same reason.

Four of the ten arrive carrying a combo tag. Three of those tags read 'needs a stack scenario' and one is verified — and the verified one resolved to a drawn game rather than a win. An unresolved ceiling is a promissory note. Price the four accordingly and read the six without tags as the settled arithmetic on the sheet.

And none of the ten moves the number. Every entry reads bracket 4 before and 4 after, and not one of them is a Game Changer. Whatever conversation this deck has about its power level, this list is not what changes it.
mana_base:
Thirty-five land copies across twenty-four entries, twelve of them tapped. That is 34% against a one-in-three budget — a hair over, and the audit flags it. Only seven come in tapped unconditionally; the other five are check lands and battle lands that pass their own test once basics are down. Counted strictly, seven taplands sits inside the ceiling of eight a slow deck gets.

The disagreement is between what the deck spends and what it holds. Green writes 56.2% of the pips on 40.0% of the sources. Red runs the opposite book — 19.8% of the pips on 32.0% of the sources — and white sits nearly square at 24.0% on 28.0%. Fifty-four green pips across 38 cards is the whole story.

Against Karsten's 36-source yardstick the totals are 26 green, 20 red, 20 white: sixteen short in the two worst colours. Thirty-six per colour is 108 sources in a 99-card deck; nobody arrives there. Watch the gap between colours instead, and the gap is red and white.

Lands alone put the pips on schedule 58.0% of the time in green, 44.6% in red and 37.3% in white. Fold in five rocks and three dorks and it becomes 74.2%, 58.0% and 58.0%. White gains twenty points off six nonland sources — there, the rocks are most of the mana base. Total sources reach 48 against Burgess's 42, thirteen of them persistent nonland producers, and the deck needs every one: the land-drop rate slides from 89.4% at turn three to 52.6% at six and 36.2% at ten while mean available mana still climbs from 5.486 to 7.321. After turn six this deck rides the rocks.

Two of the twenty-four land entries count for no colour here: restricted mana counts for nothing under this maths. Secluded Courtyard and Unclaimed Territory both show up as zeroes. They are not the same card: deck-facts reads Courtyard as paying ability costs and Territory as spells-only, which matters on any turn Belbe's Portal or Monster Manual wants activating.
threat_assessment:
They see {5}{R}{G}{W} and relax. Let them: mean cast 7.362, median 7, and 2,299 of 10,000 games never cast him by turn ten. THE EIGHT-MANA CLIMB is six turns of land drops and rocks — ramp or fixing is drawn by turn six in 84.1% of games, mean turn 2.507 — so make the quiet play and say nothing.

Run the pregame yourself. The floor is 3 on one driver, two Game Changers: Enlightened Tutor and Worldly Tutor. No two-card infinite, no mass land denial.

The read starts with the reducers. Only Otepec Huntmaster, Urza's Incubator and Knight of the Stampede cut a command-zone cast, and all three together make him {R}{G}{W}. An Incubator naming Dinosaur on an empty board is a confession; play a reducer the turn you can also play a body. Selvala, Heart of the Wilds and Regal Behemoth are the other tell — Selvala taps for your greatest power, Behemoth adds a mana per land tap while you hold the crown — so hold them for the cast turn and take the monarchy only when you can keep it.

Three signals flip you to archenemy. Rogue's Passage or Kessig Wolf Run untapped with eight mana open. A Dinosaur payoff on the table before him — Pantlaza, Sun-Favored, Garruk's Uprising, Vaultborn Tyrant, Earthshaker Dreadmaw. And the connection itself: stack 001 turns one hit into four Dinosaurs, three cards and a discover. The goldfish fires it 1.953 times a game because nothing there blocks; Forge, 40 games, gave 42 reveals off 60 attacks.

Two cards look like an engine and are not. Trapjaw Tyrant and Wrathful Raptors convert damage dealt to your own Dinosaurs, and nothing in the 99 supplies that damage for free. What Wrathful does is verified once: Blasphemous Act through Temple Altisaur, 16 at a player (stack 004), both halves drawn in 8.1% of games. Cast neither converter as a plan; cast them as bodies that make the table's own wipe cost them something.

The turn before your swing decides it. Three boxes: he is castable, a board-wide instant is in hand, and one seat cannot block or answer profitably. Protection is held by turn six in 51.1% of games; the other half, build and wait. Tapped out for eight, Flawless Maneuver is the one of your five protection instants you can cast for nothing. Assume a seat holding up four holds a sweeper — that is a stated assumption about their deck, not a read of their hand — and count the open mana before you swing.

When all three tick, take the seat. Kill by turn 8 is 0.617 with no blockers; with blockers, Forge gave 12 wins in 35 decided games.
matchups:
VS SWEEPER CONTROL — the reveal is the wave, so your board lands in one package and a wipe takes the dorks with it. Hold Flawless Maneuver over the tap-out turn: with him out it is the one of your five protection instants that costs nothing. Swing only into a tapped-out seat; a control seat holding up four is assumed to hold a wrath, and say so at the table. Land drops fall to 55.5% by turn six on 5.96 mean mana, so Nature's Lore, Kodama's Reach and Skyshroud Claim before the Signets — a land survives the sweep, a Signet under Austere Command does not. Leave him in the zone until the wrath is spent; each recast adds {2}. The rebuild is Pantlaza, Sun-Favored: a discover off any Dinosaur entering, once a turn, no combat step, no eight mana.

VS FASTER COMBO — be the beatdown from turn one. Six spot answers, two sweepers, no counterspell: Swords to Plowshares and Path to Exile go at the enabler on sight, because an answer held for something scarier stopped nothing. Your clock is kill by turn 8 in 61.7% of goldfish games, mean 8.03; theirs is shorter. Keep the hand with a reducer, attack a turn early, and spend {4} on Rogue's Passage the first turn he can swing rather than the turn it is safe.

VS STAX AND TAX — a tax on an eight-drop is the worst tax at the table, so play the doors instead. Belbe's Portal, Monster Manual and Huatli's saga put Dinosaurs onto the battlefield without a cast, and Descendants' Path casts one free off the top each upkeep. Budget the mana: Unclaimed Territory pays creature spells only and cannot activate the Portal or the Manual; Secluded Courtyard's clause says 'or activate an ability' and can. Thrashing Brontodon and Beast Within go at whatever taxes creature entry; Austere Command's artifact mode clears a sphere board while your Dinosaurs stand.

VS GO-WIDE AGGRO — let them commit. Blasphemous Act costs a mana less per creature on the battlefield, and Temple Altisaur makes it one-sided: your other Dinosaurs are dealt 1, the Altisaur takes 13 and dies, and Wrathful Raptors throws the wreckage at a face — 16 on stack 004's board. Both halves are drawn in 8.1% of games, 29.9% with a tutor, so build without it and fetch the Altisaur only when you already hold the Act. Kinjalli's Sunwing is the cheaper answer that stays: their creatures enter tapped, and a tapped creature cannot block the turn it lands. Trapjaw Tyrant is a body here, not a turret; its exile needs damage you pay for — the Act, Zacama's {2}{R}, Itzquinth's {2}.
editors_letter:
The deck is named after the Dinosaur on the cover. The engine is a Human with three toughness who is not invited to a single one of the parties this deck throws.

That sentence is why Gishath, Sun's Avatar got an issue. On top is the plan everyone can see: six or seven turns of quiet land-playing under an eight-mana Avatar who, when he connects, turns combat damage into a fistful of Dinosaurs pulled off the top of your own library and dropped straight onto the table. Underneath it runs a second machine that needs none of that — shoot your own board for one point, and four creatures turn a scratch into a card, a land, an exile and a fresh 5/5. The scratch wipes off at end of turn. You paid nothing.

You will have a good time here if you like the long sit, if you enjoy hurting your own creatures on purpose, and if you can be patient with a commander who is expensive and honest about it. You will not, if you need your commander to be your plan. Ledger has the cast turn, and it is no comfort.

Coach Brightside opens the log by naming the card to mulligan for, and it is not the one on the cover. The Counselor spends the rest of the page keeping him inside what has been proved — and the most interesting sentence in this file is that nobody has yet resolved a board of these Dinosaurs killing anybody. Read that as an invitation.

pilots_log.text: Nobody wants to hear this in a magazine with a seven-foot Avatar on the cover, but here it is: the card you mulligan for is the 1/3 Human. Forerunner of the Empire, four mana, and it is the only thing in this list that shoots your own board for free and can do it again next turn. The punchline is that your commander can never hand it to you — his trigger only free-rolls Dinosaurs, and your engine is a Human Soldier.

On the record, and then narrower than the Coach put it.

Two of this deck's five passing stacks open with that Human's trigger, and neither of them has the commander on the board at all. Stack 005: one optional ping, four enrage triggers, five things bought. Stack 003: the same ping run three times, ending at seven Polyraptor tokens. His reading of the commander's trigger is correct as text, too — it puts Dinosaur creature cards onto the battlefield and the rest on the bottom of your library, and Forerunner of the Empire is a Human Soldier, so the reveal cannot find him.

What the record does not do is rank your cards. Stack 001 is on the record as well, and it is the largest single event in this file: seven combat damage, that many cards revealed, three of your Dinosaurs onto the battlefield alongside the Regisaur Alpha token, three draws off Garruk's Uprising, and one Pantlaza discover at X of six. That is not the play of a card anybody should apologise for.

Plainly: the Coach has named the engine that runs without eight mana. He has not named a better card, because nothing in this file measures better.

The Coach's card against the Coach's commander, in figures.

Commander cast turn: mean 7.969, median 8. Cast by turn six in 8.3% of ten thousand seeded runs. Not cast at all by turn ten in 5,533 of them. Among the runs where he is cast, turn eight is the mode at 1,332; the largest bucket in the whole histogram is 'never'. The simulation models no cost reduction, so Otepec Huntmaster and Urza's Incubator are absent from those numbers. That is a floor on the problem, not the expectation.

The enrage converters: 60.8% assembled, 50.6% by turn six, mean turn 3.053.

And the figure the Coach's plan actually needs does not exist. The declaration groups five converters and names no damage source, so no run has ever measured a converter and a source on the board in the same game. I can tell you 50.6%. I cannot tell you what share of those games held anything to pull the trigger.

Then play the turn you can have. Here it is, and it ends with you saying no.

Forerunner is out, a Dinosaur walks in, and the trigger asks whether you want to shoot everything. Yes. One damage to every creature on the table, yours very much included, and now count what you just bought: their token is dead, Trapjaw Tyrant exiles their 3/3, Ripjaw Raptor draws you a card, Ranging Raptors goes and gets a Forest, Polyraptor makes another Polyraptor. Then that copy walks in and the trigger asks again.

Say no. You already have everything. Nothing of yours died, the scratches come off at end of turn, and a second sweep buys you nothing you are not already holding. Take the five and pass the turn. The best button in this deck is the one you decline to press.

That is stack 005 exactly, and the parts the Coach skipped are the parts worth owning.

The choice is made on resolution — CR 603.5, 'The choice is made when the ability resolves.' You are not committing to a sweep when the trigger goes on the stack. You look at the board the first one produced and then decide about the next one.

Sequence matters twice more. State-based actions are performed before waiting triggers go on the stack (CR 704.3), so the opponent's 1/1 was already destroyed and gone when Trapjaw's trigger took a target, which left their 3/3 as the only legal one. And CR 120.6: damage marked on a creature remains until the cleanup step. That is the entire economy of this deck. You are spending a resource that expires by itself, which is why the schematic has no fodder stage — nothing is being fed to anything. Your creatures get scratched, and the scratches go away.

One correction to the Coach's ledger. Forerunner takes the point as well, one of three, and it has no enrage and it is not a Dinosaur. It pays and it is not paid.

The body sets the bound. Three toughness, one damage a sweep: three sweeps and the source is in the graveyard. That is stack 003, where the Human dies to its own third ping.

Seven tokens is the maximum that stack reaches. Yes at every link returns six. The larger number requires declining one trigger in the middle.

Ten arrows in the engine schematic. Four of them rest on a passing stack. Two of the four carry damage: one is the ping, the other is Blasphemous Act pointed at your own board.

All right — but eight Polyraptors is eight Polyraptors, and Garruk's Uprising has already handed the whole team trample. I untap, I cast Overwhelming Stampede, I point everything at the seat that cannot block it. Counselor, before I do this at a table with witnesses: on the record, does that kill somebody?

No — and I want to be exact about which kind of no this is. It is not 'the maths fails'. It is 'nobody has checked'.

Not one of the five passing stacks resolves combat damage to a player. The stage is called ONE SWING, AND NOBODY HAS MEASURED IT, and the title is doing honest work: it has one arrow in and one arrow out and both are drawn dashed, which is this magazine's way of saying a competent analyst believes it and no checker has read it.

What I can give you is the one measured attack on a life total in this file, and it is not combat. Stack 004: Blasphemous Act with Temple Altisaur on the board. Thirteen to every creature at once; the shield prevents all but one for each other Dinosaur you control and does nothing whatever for Altisaur itself, which is not 'another Dinosaur' relative to itself, so it eats the full thirteen and dies. Wrathful Raptors then triggers once per damaged Dinosaur — CR 603.2c, one event containing several occurrences — for thirteen, one, one and one. Every opposing creature had already been destroyed by state-based actions before those triggers chose targets, so the only legal targets left were players. Sixteen at one seat: twenty-six to ten.

The holding: this deck has proved a cascade, a ping web, a bounded token burst and a one-sided sweep. It has not proved a kill. Swing if you like. I will not let you tell the table it is lethal.

Board size, for the swing she will not certify. Mean creatures in play: 2.706 at turn six, 3.892 at turn eight, 5.066 at turn ten. Mean available mana at turn six, 5.486.

The sweep she just walked through assembles in 2.5% of ten thousand runs and 1.4% by turn six, mean turn 5.462. It is the lowest-rated pairing measured on this deck, and each half alone is 7.1% of an opening seven.

The class that does show up is the runway: ramp or fixing, 93.9% assembled, 86.9% by turn six, mean turn 2.044. Land drops hit 89.4% on turn three and 52.6% by turn six.

Taken. And it changes nothing about how you play on Tuesday.

You are not sitting on a hand waiting for a certificate. You are taking value turns: ping, draw, ramp, exile, another 5/5, pass. Do that three times and the board nobody has measured builds itself while the table is busy with somebody else. Then you swing, because swinging is how the game ends.

What you do have to do is keep the Human breathing. Hold the board-wide instants for the 1/3, not for the 7/6. And take some comfort in this: the table is going to look across at a seven-foot Avatar and a little Human Soldier and shoot the wrong one. Let them.

Notice what that instruction costs him, because the deck's furniture was built for the other creature.

Temple Altisaur's shield reads 'another Dinosaur you control'. Forerunner is a Human Soldier, so it is not for him — and stack 004 already establishes how literally that clause reads. Secluded Courtyard and Unclaimed Territory produce coloured mana only for the chosen creature type. The commander's reveal cannot find him. On the text, Descendants' Path could put him onto the battlefield, but only while you already control a Human or a Soldier, since the shared type there cannot be Dinosaur.

And the shield the Coach wants held. Flawless Maneuver is free only if you control a commander — in the majority of games, which is to say in exactly the games where the Human is the plan, it costs {2}{W} like any other trick. Whether any of those five instants has in fact kept him alive is unchecked. Nobody has run it.

Plainly: the engine of this deck is the one creature none of its protection was written for.

Rates for the cover. Protection held for the board is five instants: 59.0% assembled, 48.5% by turn six. Temple Altisaur is not in that group.

White is the narrowest of the three by sources: twenty against a thirty-six-source yardstick, on-curve rate 0.58. Red is 0.58, green 0.742. Wakening Sun's Avatar asks for three white pips.

And on mulligans, since the Coach opened on one. Keep rate on the first seven is 77.1%, mean mulligans 0.28. One named card is 7.1% of an opening seven. He is asking you to mulligan toward a 7.1%.

I am, and I would do it again.

So here is your game. Turns one through four you play lands and you are nobody's problem. Then the Human arrives and you stop being nobody's problem: ping once, take the five things, decline the second trigger, pass. Do it again next turn. Keep a board-wide instant in hand for the little guy.

And when the Avatar does land — Ledger has told you how often, and you heard him — you do not cast him into a clean board and hope. You give him a reason to connect, you take the reveal, and you count the Dinosaurs that fall out of the top of your library.

Then you swing. Nobody has certified that swing yet. Go and be the reason they have to.
